instrumento: the rear monitor of a cinema camera rigged on a gimbal
escena: SCENE (documentary, a real photograph during a content shoot in a small, dark studio set in Santiago): we look over the shoulder of the camera operator, who is entirely out of frame except for a blurred edge of a sleeve, straight into the bright rear monitor of a compact cinema camera on a gimbal. Inside the monitor, razor sharp: the take itself, a vertical 9:16 frame of a can of BRÍO, a fictitious Chilean sparkling citrus soda, sweating with cold droplets on a slab of dark stone: a slim glossy can in deep cobalt blue with the bold white wordmark «BRÍO» running vertically up the can in a rounded sans-serif, the accent on the «Í», and a small white sun symbol above it; the same BRÍO can stands for real on the set beyond the monitor, caught at the instant a hand closes around it and lifts it a few millimetres off the stone, side light, with the framing guides of the monitor overlaid as thin white lines. Beyond the monitor, out of focus, the real set: the same stone slab and can under one small softbox, a matte black flag, a coiled cable, and an LED tube glowing cool blue at the back of the set. ONE tiny point on the monitor, the record indicator, glows vivid orange (#FF6500), the only warm accent in the frame. The monitor's own glow lights the gimbal handles and the operator's out-of-focus sleeve. Camera about sixty centimetres behind the monitor, 50mm f/1.8, the monitor frame filling the centre of the picture. Current-generation equipment only, nothing vintage. Real sensor grain, genuine depth of field. The only lettering in the frame is the «BRÍO» wordmark on the can, spelled exactly B-R-Í-O; no other readable text, no logos of any real brand on the can, the camera or the monitor.

lecho.objeto: the dark out-of-focus rubber grip of the gimbal handle crossing the bottom of the frame, outside the monitor's glow
